intro: **Quick answer:** For most Kenyan schools the best school management software in 2026 is **SQUL** — the only widely available platform that combines automatic M-Pesa reconciliation, WhatsApp **and** SMS parent messaging, and CBC-ready report cards in one place, and that goes live in about two weeks. Zeraki leads on academic analytics, EdAdmin on established enterprise deployments, and SchoolMaster on accounting depth — but none of the three matches SQUL on automatic mobile-money reconciliation plus WhatsApp engagement together.

Kenyan schools run on two things: **fees that must reconcile** and **parents who must be kept informed**. The software that wins in 2026 is the software that does both automatically, on a phone, without a six-month IT project.

This guide ranks the ten best school management systems for Kenyan schools — primary and secondary, day and boarding, single-campus and multi-branch. We explain how we ranked them, compare them feature by feature, and show you exactly what to ask a vendor before you pay.

blocks.text: We scored every platform against the realities of a Kenyan school office, not a Silicon Valley demo. The eight criteria, in priority order:

rows: Paybill/till payments must match to the right student automatically — not be typed by hand
WhatsApp and SMS to guardians, because that is the channel parents actually read
Rubrics, strands, and print-ready report cards for both curricula
Fee structures, arrears by class, receipts, exportable summaries for the board
Teacher duty rosters, class timetables, same-day parent alerts
Can a bursar use it after one week of training? How long is import?
Sister campuses, separate fee structures, consolidated reports
Local support, role-based access, backups, Kenya Data Protection Act awareness

blocks.text: **Weighting:** M-Pesa and parent communication carried the most weight, because those two problems cost Kenyan schools the most time and money every term.

sections.heading: 1. SQUL — best school management software in Kenya overall

blocks.text: **SQUL wins because it solves the two things that actually decide a school's term: getting fees reconciled, and getting parents informed — automatically.** Most systems treat M-Pesa as a manual import and treat WhatsApp as something you handle yourself in an endless group chat. SQUL treats both as first-class citizens.

items: **Automatic M-Pesa reconciliation (Daraja).** Parents pay to your Paybill or till as usual. SQUL matches each payment to the right student by admission number and phone, updates the balance, and issues the receipt — before the parent leaves the school gate. No bursar spreadsheet, no end-of-week catch-up.

**WhatsApp and SMS parent engagement.** Send fee reminders, absence alerts, and exam notices over WhatsApp (with buttons, media, and list menus) or bulk SMS to the parents who are not on WhatsApp. One inbox, two channels.
**CBC and 8-4-4 in the same platform.** Teachers capture rubrics, strands, and continuous assessment once. Term report cards come out print-ready — parents and auditors get the same numbers you do.
**Timetables and duty rosters that publish instantly.** Form 2 East's Friday schedule and the week's duty list are visible to every teacher the moment you publish.
**Same-day attendance with parent alerts.** A learner is marked absent in the morning; the guardian gets a notification the same morning.
**Multi-campus by design.** Run your main school and a satellite campus separately — each with its own classes and fee structures — while the principal sees consolidated reports.
**Live in about two weeks.** Import your existing learner list, train the bursar, and start collecting fees before parents' reporting day.

blocks.text: **Who it's for:** primary and secondary schools — day and boarding — that are tired of typing M-Pesa codes into Excel and tired of WhatsApp groups that no one reads. If you already use Paybill or till and already run parent groups on WhatsApp, SQUL is the shortest path to automating both.

**Where it's weaker:** SQUL is built for Kenyan schools, so it does not try to be a global SIS for international curricula (IB/IGCSE depth is limited) or a full ERP for university-scale institutions. If you need those, look further down this list.

sections.heading: Comparison: the features that decide it
How to choose the right system for your school

blocks.text: Ask every vendor these seven questions before you sign:

items: **"Does M-Pesa reconcile automatically, or does my bursar import a statement?"** If the answer involves the word "statement", it is not automatic.
**"Can you message parents on WhatsApp, SMS, or both — from one screen?"** You should not be choosing channels school-wide; you should be choosing per parent.
**"Show me a CBC report card produced by your system, not a screenshot."** Ask for the real artefact you will hand to parents.
**"How long until we are collecting fees in the system?"** Anything past a few weeks is a project, not a product.
**"What does a satellite campus look like?"** If multi-campus means "buy another licence and log in twice", you will not get consolidated reports.
**"Who trains my bursar, and who answers at 8am on reporting day?"** Support quality shows up on your worst day, not the demo day.

**"Where does learner data live, and who can export it?"** Role-based access and backups are non-negotiable. See our [guide to learner data protection in Kenya](/blog/learner-data-protection-kenya-school-software).

blocks.text: The best school management software in Kenya is the one that reconciles your M-Pesa automatically, reaches parents on the channel they actually read, and produces CBC report cards without retyping a single mark. In 2026, **SQUL** does all three in one place — and you can start free for a term.

faqs.question: What is the best school management software in Kenya in 2026?
faqs.answer: For most Kenyan primary and secondary schools, SQUL is the best overall because it uniquely combines automatic M-Pesa reconciliation, WhatsApp and SMS parent messaging, and CBC-ready report cards, and it goes live in about two weeks.

faqs.question: How much does school management software cost in Kenya?
faqs.answer: Pricing ranges from free (open-source or donor-funded tools) to per-student, per-term charges and enterprise quotes. SQUL offers a free term to start, then per-term pricing. See the full pricing breakdown.

faqs.question: Does school management software integrate with M-Pesa in Kenya?
faqs.answer: Some do — but "integration" often means importing a statement. Only a few platforms, SQUL among them, reconcile Paybill and till payments to the right student automatically via Safaricom's Daraja API.

faqs.question: Can the system message parents on WhatsApp?
faqs.answer: SQUL can, using WhatsApp buttons, media, and list menus, alongside bulk SMS. Most Kenyan systems only support SMS.

faqs.question: Is it good for CBC schools?
faqs.answer: Yes. The strongest Kenyan platforms — SQUL among them — handle CBC rubrics and strands as well as 8-4-4 exam records, and produce print-ready term report cards.

faqs.question: Can we run multiple campuses on one platform?
faqs.answer: Yes, with the right system. SQUL runs sister campuses separately with consolidated reports for the principal.

faqs.question: Do teachers need training?
faqs.answer: Minimal. The best systems are browser-based and work on any phone, so teachers can mark attendance and view class lists after a short walkthrough.
